### Row `ModifyingUDS`

| Field | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Category_12_A3CA532A4207111301CC0DB004E1A0F4` | `int32` | `0` |
| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "77E7E7A74727928BA03E71B5FBEAE33A", "You may have a need to alter some blueprint logic within a UDS class or add your own. If this is needed, I recommend doing your modifications to a child of the class in question. That way your work is not lost when you need to update UDS.\r\n\r\nTo make a child of a blueprint class, just right click on the class in the content browser and select Create Child Blueprint Class.\r\n\r\nIn that child class, you can override individual functions to replace or add to their existing logic. For example, in a child of the UDS class, you might override the Current Sun Light Color function to replace the logic which determines the color of the sun light.\r\n\r\nSome classes have empty functions which are just there for you to override in child classes. For example the Weather Override Volume has its Custom Volume Behavior function."))` |
| `EntryTitle_4_4B2C1546415E1329EC06F8B28CB05DF9` | `FText` | `NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "345C0C644E8C839206E81593A8B91055", "Modifying UDS Blueprints")` |

### Row `MoonAppearance`

| Field | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Category_12_A3CA532A4207111301CC0DB004E1A0F4` | `int32` | `0` |
| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "AEFB004849AA0D9B1E56D7B440A3AB48", "The Moon category is where you\'ll find all the settings specifically for the appearance and phase of the moon.\r\n\r\nBy default, the moon supports rendering moon phases, which can be adjusted with the Moon Phase setting. You can also enable an option in the Moon category to have moon phase change over time. Note that if using Simulate Real Moon, the moon phase will be set by the simulation.\r\n\r\nYou can change out the moon texture as well from the moon category, but note that there are two textures for that. The one called Moon Texture is the RGB color and alpha channel of the moon. The one called Moon Phase Normal is an RGB texture containing the local normal of the moon, for rendering moon phases. If you want to replace the moon with a texture that doesn\'t require moon phases, you can disable phase rendering entirely with the setting Render Moon Phases."))` |
| `EntryTitle_4_4B2C1546415E1329EC06F8B28CB05DF9` | `FText` | `NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "697E4E2A42220C5E782BCEAAC75B193F", "Moon Appearance and Phase")` |

### Row `OnscreenControls`

| Field | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Category_12_A3CA532A4207111301CC0DB004E1A0F4` | `int32` | `0` |
| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "1A0FAC44445933F7CF576FB3D18B3B98", "If your project needs a simple on screen interface to give the user control of time and/or weather, UDS comes with a widget built to be a good quick and clean solution for that.\r\n\r\nIt\'s called UDS Onscreen Controls and it can be found in the widget designer palette in the Ultra Dynamic Sky Widgets category.\r\n\r\nBy default, all of its controls will be enabled, but you can use the exposed settings on the widget details to turn off the controls you don\'t need. For example, you could limit it to only Show Time Control, for a simple compact control for Time of Day.\r\n\r\nThere are also settings to control the time and date format displayed, and the weather presets available in the weather controls.\r\n\r\nIf you want to use the Onscreen Controls on a client in a multiplayer context, to control UDS/UDW state on the server, there is support for this. In your player controller class, add the UDS Client Controller component. Onscreen Controls will automatically use this from clients to replicate time/weather functions up to the server."))` |
| `EntryTitle_4_4B2C1546415E1329EC06F8B28CB05DF9` | `FText` | `NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "0D5165B14DAD47D940C06585248A37C9", "On Screen Sky Controls")` |
| `Keywords_8_5ACC585649ABDE1192D0EAB5258A2665` | `TArray` | `("onscreen controls","time of day slider","slider","widget","buttons","hud","time slider","menu")` |

### Row `OptimizePerformance`

| Field | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Category_12_A3CA532A4207111301CC0DB004E1A0F4` | `int32` | `0` |
| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "304B41884A542AEFA9276A820221B003", "Here are some of the most performance relevant settings to take note of if you want to reduce the performance cost of the main UDS features.\r\n\r\nNote this focuses on the cost of UDS\' features, not general engine/renderer features which aren\'t specific to UDS. General UE resources on optimizing performance of engine features (dynamic shadows, global illumination, etc) will apply the same when using UDS."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "D2D69F344E081BA05A9A37A01A6B136D", "^Sky Mode"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "5FF04FAE4430F756FB7DCE93447CEF96", ">The most GPU performance relevant setting on the whole system is certainly [Sky_Mode;skymode] . The most expensive option here is of course [Volumetric_Clouds;volumetricclouds] . [2D_Dynamic_Clouds_;2ddynamicclouds] is significantly cheaper to render, and [Static_Clouds_;staticclouds] is somewhat cheaper still. No Clouds obviously has the most minimal cost (outside of the [Space_;spacemode] mode)."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "C6EC67DD4CD17A27968854B018A6D9D9", "^Color Mode"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "34952DD448C5E1F723A683B026ED5564", ">[Color_Mode_;colormode] can be changed to [Simplified_Color_;simplifiedcolor] to reduce some of the sky rendering cost, by disabling the [sky_atmosphere;skyatmosphere] , and using simpler material logic for the sky colors."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "B108F3CE4C85953CABCBA485B382B67B", "^Project Mode"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "19293A724E684FD413510AB8504809B9", ">If real-time performance is at all required, make absolutely certain [Project_Mode_;projectmode] is set to \"Game / Real-Time\". The Cinematic option is for offline rendering only, and applies quality settings at [runtime_;runtime] which will severely impact performance."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "41E5A3E34265039A4EBCD9ABC18D6E79", "^Volumetric Clouds"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "B3B6084E48E6CF61A0F7D2AF8889A57C", ">[Volumetric_Cloud_Rendering_Mode_;volcloudrendermode] - Has an effect on the cost of the cloud rendering. If looking to minimize the performance cost of the clouds on the GPU, make sure to use either of the modes which favor performance.\r\n\r\nView Sample Scale and Shadow Sample Scale - Reducing these will lower the cost of the volumetric rendering, but can introduce noise and artifacts.\r\n\r\nMax High Frequency Noise Levels - Increasing this above the default will increase cost of cloud rendering when close or zoomed into clouds, how much depending on the High Frequency Noise Distance Scale setting.\r\n\r\nTwo Layers - This option requires a much higher sample count for the volumetric clouds to resolve both layers, as wel as a slightly more complex volumetric material."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "E9C0CD4942D9390FDC5E778CFAA7E575", "^2D Dynamic Clouds"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "F35B167C43354E26CC4C12B663991640", ">One Cloud Layer - Enabling this will reduce the cost of the sky shader somewhat with 2D clouds. Note that One Cloud Layer is already enabled on the material level at Low material quality."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "5C2C855C4D9A895DBC16349BF6EA0A26", "^Sky Light"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "CD685E3C41E972B29D09BC934B925C09", ">[Sky_Light_Mode_;skylightmode] can have some small effect on performance, due to the cost of real time sky light capture. To eliminate that cost, but still have the sky light adapt to changing time and weather, try using the mode called \"Cubemap with Dynamic Color Tinting\"."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "11B4775F4D909F755939C3A3948DF1FB", "^Volumetric Fog"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "5ADCEF694408BF8723F25D8EC566FF12", ">Note that enabling volumetric fog has a very significant rendering cost. In addition, UDS\' own option to enable its global volumetric material will increase that cost somewhat.\r\n\r\nVolumetric Fog, being a rendering feature of the engine, gets its scalability settings from the Shadow Quality scalability group. Note that by default, the engine\'s scalability settings for Low and Medium quality disable volumetric fog entirely."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "05F4D2FE4E118F5F2CB9EDA7E2FC4761", "^Miscellaneous Performance Tips"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "4FF08A0445C30DB5687E328DA48AC9A6", ">- Almost all of UDS\' materials respond in some way to global material quality level, reducing material complexity when using Low or Medium quality materials.\r\n\r\n- All of the lights on UDS are movable by default, but static or stationary lighting is always going to be a more performance friendly option if it can fit your project. See the entry in this document on static lighting for more info on setting that up with UDS\' lights.\r\n\r\n- By default, UDS and UDW will do their tick logic every other frame, above a default framerate threshold of 45. The option for this is Half Rate Tick, in the Scalability/Performance category. I would recommend leaving this enabled, but if you need the blueprints to tick every frame, you can disable it there. Potentially you could also lower the framerate threshold to let this optimization apply at 30fps, but note fast changes to lighting/sky properties will at that point be updating at only 15fps, and can be visibly stuttery.\r\n\r\n- You can also set the Sky Mode to change on launch with the current Effects Quality set in the Game User Settings. For example, you could make it so that settings Medium and above use volumetric clouds, while Low will use static clouds. You can do this by enabling \"Use Sky Mode Scalability Map\" in the Scalability / Performance category, and adjusting the map.\r\n\r\n- If you want to limit how often the directional lights on UDS update as they move, to reduce the frequency that cached directional shadows need updating, there are settings specifically for that. They are the Lights Update settings in the Directional Light category."))` |

### Row `Paint_Volumetric_Clouds`

| Field | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Category_12_A3CA532A4207111301CC0DB004E1A0F4` | `int32` | `0` |
| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "3423D0CD48AA45EFE73ABFB03B2AE61E", "There are tools included for manually painting cloud coverage into the [volumetric_cloud_;volumetricclouds] layer. This painted coverage level is applied on top of the global [Cloud_Coverage_;udscloudcoverage] value set on UDS (or by the weather state if UDW is present).\r\n\r\nWith UDS in the scene and Volumetric Clouds selected for its sky mode, run the Volumetric Cloud Painter from the Ultra Dynamic Sky dropdown on the level editor toolbar, or by running the editor utility asset in the Blueprints folder.\r\n\r\nAn actor called a UDS Cloud Paint Container is what holds the painting data this tool creates. When starting the painter, you can make a new container, or if your level already has one, open an existing one. You can have as many containers as you want in your level. See the section below about changing between them.\r\n\r\nHere\'s a description of the various parts of the cloud painter interface and how to use them:"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "BCCD207F4418CB524F55CB94A8F67B44", ">- The top bar is where you will adjust the brush used to paint cloud coverage. You can change the texture, strength, falloff, and brush spacing.\r\n\r\n- The viewport in the cloud painter is where you will paint brush strokes onto the cloud layer. Left click to paint, right click to drag the viewport, middle mouse click and drag to zoom in and out (or use the buttons in the lower right). You can change between three view modes by clicking View in the lower left. You can also toggle the painting viewport locking the level viewport camera to the painting area, using the lock icon there.\r\n\r\n- On the left of the viewport are the different paint and erase modes. You can paint three levels of cloud coverage, represented on the viewport as red, green, and blue. You can also erase existing painting (paint black).\r\n\r\n- At the bottom of the tool is the button to Save to Textures. Make sure to press this to end your painting session and save your work. It will save the painted cells to texture files. It will put these into a subfolder called UDS_LevelData, in the folder where the level is located."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "A592D91F4983039BC4BF899A637D4644", "The painted cell textures are drawn into a cloud coverage render target on UDS. You can find the settings for the size and resolution of that target, and how its used, on UDS in the Volumetric Cloud Painting category."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "6D07C02540838C938E206CB2CFE36992", "^Changing Between Multiple Cloud Paint Containers"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "D586AC2D4D84CFD9C33CE29C1173BD56", ">If you have multiple cloud paint containers in your level, and you want to change which one is active, you should call the Activate and Deactivate functions on the actor. You can call this at runtime, or from the details panel in the editor."))` |
| `EntryTitle_4_4B2C1546415E1329EC06F8B28CB05DF9` | `FText` | `NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "838A73374BC2E87EA1CCDDB56C35E01F", "Painting Volumetric Cloud Coverage")` |
| `Keywords_8_5ACC585649ABDE1192D0EAB5258A2665` | `TArray` | `("volumetric clouds","paint","cloud painting","draw","drawing","painting","painter","cloud coverage")` |

### Row `PathTracer`

| Field | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Category_12_A3CA532A4207111301CC0DB004E1A0F4` | `int32` | `0` |
| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "7F680C34481F4E768C70A99A61873800", "If you turn on the [Path_Tracer_;pathtracer] in a scene with Ultra Dynamic Sky, you\'ll face some rendering limitations of the path tracer. The path tracer uses the sky light cube map as a replacement for native sky rendering.\r\n\r\nUltra Dynamic Sky has a setting specifically to adjust for these limitations as well as it can, to work acceptably as a background for path traced renders. Just enable the option \"Adjust for Path Tracer\" in the Cinematics / Offline Rendering category on UDS.\r\n\r\nAlso note the setting \"Render Height Fog In Path Tracer Using Post Process\" in the Fog Color category. This is enabled by default, and allows the path tracer to render an approximation of distant height fog, which the path tracer lacks native support for."))` |

### Row `PlayerOcclusion`

| Field | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Category_12_A3CA532A4207111301CC0DB004E1A0F4` | `int32` | `0` |
| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "73B9C45F44597628791B92AA6F7079C1", "Player Occlusion is the name of a system on UDS which can actively monitor how occluded from the sky/weather the player camera/pawn is within interiors. In other words, how \"inside\" or \"outside\" the player is in relation to the scene collision around them.\r\n\r\nThe resulting occlusion values are utilized by features on the sky and weather:"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "EA2C2293468D4170A36B33B9845524AA", ">- Interior Adjustments on UDS, which can adjust some sky properties based on occlusion.\r\n- Sound Occlusion on UDW, which can quiet/muffle weather sounds when the player is occluded.\r\n- Temperature calculation on UDW can optionally apply an interior temperature when occluded."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "C75906A24A86D84D3FAFA3865AA4C32E", "The Player Occlusion category on UDS contains the settings which define how occlusion values are determined. How much time each occlusion update takes, how many collision traces are used, what collision channel is traced against, etc.\r\n\r\nTo direct player occlusion values in specific spaces, you can place a UDS Occlusion Volume actor into your level."))` |

### Row `PlayerWeatherReact`

| Field | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Category_12_A3CA532A4207111301CC0DB004E1A0F4` | `int32` | `1` |
| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "C9FC14414AE752781262CAB324F11A14", "Actor Weather Status is a component you can add to an actor which will keep track of its direct exposure to weather, as well as its temperature and wind exposure. This is intended for important actors like the player pawn which may need to constantly monitor their individual status with regard to weather.\r\n\r\nAt [runtime;runtime] , this component will use periodic traces to test the actor\'s weather exposure and keep track of how its temperature is affected by that exposure. All of these values can be found in the component\'s Status category.\r\n\r\nThe Actor Weather Status component also has its own [event_dispatchers;eventdispatcher] , for when the actor itself is exposed to rain, or snow, or its temperature goes past thresholds for hot and cold.\r\n\r\nYou can also add dynamic material instances to an array in the component\'s Material Effects category, to have parameters set using the status values. These parameters are all 0-1 values and are called \"Wet\", \"Raining\", \"Snowy\", \"Dusty\", and \"Wind Intensity\". The UDW material functions have an input called \"Use Local Parameters\" which is made to work with this.\r\n\r\nInstead of using an Actor Weather Status component to always track weather state, you can also do a single query of an actor\'s exposure to weather by calling \"Test Actor for Weather Exposure\" on UDW. If you have your actor call this function, and provide a reference to itself for the Actor input, the function will output floats which describe how exposed the actor is to rain, wind, snow and dust. These values each range from 0 to 1. They scale with the intensity of the weather and the amount the actor is exposed. So for example a value of 1 for snow would mean the actor is fully exposed to snow at maximum intensity."))` |
| `EntryTitle_4_4B2C1546415E1329EC06F8B28CB05DF9` | `FText` | `NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "88426F2E4B70D154FA8229BD2F345048", "Actor Weather Status")` |
| `Keywords_8_5ACC585649ABDE1192D0EAB5258A2665` | `TArray` | `("exposure","wind","snow","rain","player","actor","exposed","hit","actor weather status")` |

### Row `PostProcess`

| Field | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Category_12_A3CA532A4207111301CC0DB004E1A0F4` | `int32` | `0` |
| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "DCDDD2CF4753FB39FF65698C4357D85E", "If you want to apply post process settings which are applied dynamically depending on time or weather, UDS has a feature for that.\r\n\r\nIn the Post Processing category on UDS, you\'ll find an empty array called Post Process Components. If you add entries to this array, the system will create a post process component for each one.\r\n\r\nEach entry has post process settings, where you can override and modify any post setting such as bloom settings, color grading, vignette, etc. Below the post processing settings are:"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "D3FA283D40AB01764084B285823ED112", ">- Checkboxes to Enable/Disable this post process component based on the time of day. This will control the blend weight of the component, fading it in and out based on the current time.\r\n\r\n-  Checkboxes to mask the component with cloud coverage, fog, dust, or interior occlusion. For example, if you checked \"Mask Blend Weight When Overcast\", the post settings for this component would fade away as the sky becomes overcast.\r\n\r\n- Checkboxes to mask the component if raining/snowing or not. This is dependent on the presence of UDW. If UDW isn\'t being used, these will have no effect."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "B6BDCE4B4366DA9F60C9E4B5BAAA17BB", "By adding and customizing the entries in this array, you can create post processing settings which change for the time and weather\'s specific context."))` |
| `EntryTitle_4_4B2C1546415E1329EC06F8B28CB05DF9` | `FText` | `NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "36ED2C1E4539FC8E7915B8B25F88D740", "Post Processing")` |
| `Keywords_8_5ACC585649ABDE1192D0EAB5258A2665` | `TArray` | `("post","post process","post processing","effects","color grading")` |

### Row `PostProcessWindFog`

| Field | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Category_12_A3CA532A4207111301CC0DB004E1A0F4` | `int32` | `1` |
| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "E935184F406DDC8E023064A9E3EFC33C", "Post Process Wind Fog is an effect which adds extra fog noise in the local area around the camera, moving with the wind and weather particles. It\'s achieved using a post process effect, simpler but much more performance friendly than similar effects achieved with volumetric fog. The intensity of the effect scales with the amount of fog, rain, snow, or dust, in the current [weather_state.;weatherstate]\r\n\r\nThere are multiple methods for masking the effect in spaces blocked from weather like interiors. By default, the effect uses the Weather Occlusion Volume, a volume texture which caches exposure to weather around the camera, using the global distance field. This is the best option, but you can also change to having the effect mask using player occlusion."))` |

| Field | Type | Value |

| `Category_12_A3CA532A4207111301CC0DB004E1A0F4` | `int32` | `0` |
| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "2B5C4F664DF30293B89A4D8B897307FC", "The third top level Mode setting in Basic Controls is [Project_Mode;projectmode] . This setting determines how the system will behave at [runtime;runtime] . There are two options for Project Mode:"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "A64FD5D842938B5E002A8190BE58EA93", ">1. Game / Real-time enables runtime optimizations which spread out calculations on UDS. It\'s intended for games or any kind of project where real-time performance is needed.\r\n\r\n2. Cinematic / Offline disables these optimizations, so that everything dynamic on the sky will update fully every frame. It also increases many quality settings automatically at runtime, to maximize render quality. It\'s intended for rendering movies or stills, or any project where real-time performance is not needed."))` |

### Row `PuddleFluidVolume`

| Field | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Category_12_A3CA532A4207111301CC0DB004E1A0F4` | `int32` | `1` |
| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "51F08C16450379B82362A4B43D3AAC08", "The Puddle Fluid Volume is an actor class which can render a puddle as an actual water surface that moves up and down as the puddle fills/empties with [weather_state._;weatherstate] This is in contrast to the puddles achieved using material effects, which are just flat surface effects changing the roughness and normal of a material. A Puddle Fluid Volume is suitable for situations where there is an actual geometric recess/cavity in the ground, for water to fill.\r\n\r\nOptionally, you can also render the Puddle Fluid Volume using Puddle Fluid Interactions, which renders the puddle as a grid mesh simulating natural ripples, caused by the DLWE Interaction component contacting the water surface. (See the entry on the Dynamic Landscape Weather Effects for info on the DLWE Interaction component.) Understand, when using fluid interactions, the puddle is a dense grid of simulated particles. The size of the puddle area will have a significant effect on the cost of this simulation, and should generally be kept to small spaces/individual puddles.\r\n\r\nYou can find the Puddle Fluid Volume class in the Blueprints/Weather_Effects folder.\r\n\r\nWhen placing the actor in the level, note its current filled/dry state will be informed by the current weather you have selected on UDW. You can override this in the level editor as needed, using the setting Level Editor Preview State. You should place the puddle so that when it\'s dry, it\'s completely hidden under the ground. Note that the puddle mesh is visible in the editor when it\'s in its dry state, to help with placing the actor. But at [runtime,_;runtime] the puddle mesh will be hidden when dry.\r\n\r\nYou can scale the puddle area using the Puddle Area setting, or by scaling the actor. The actor can only be rotated on the Z axis.\r\n\r\nThe water surface is rendered using a translucent material by default, so for good reflections with Lumen, make sure to enable High Quality Translucency Reflections in your project settings.\r\n\r\nFor settings relating to how and when the puddle will be filled/emptied at runtime, see the Puddle State category.\r\n\r\nFor toggling or adjusting the behavior of the fluid interactions with DLWE Interaction components, see the Fluid Interactions category."))` |
| `EntryTitle_4_4B2C1546415E1329EC06F8B28CB05DF9` | `FText` | `NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "C589B3724D9C4CEC99FE6FB16CD28142", "Puddle Fluid Volume")` |
| `Keywords_8_5ACC585649ABDE1192D0EAB5258A2665` | `TArray` | `("puddle","water","water surface","puddle fluid volume")` |

### Row `RadialStorm`

| Field | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Category_12_A3CA532A4207111301CC0DB004E1A0F4` | `int32` | `1` |
| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "36A7A65D4AE5C85E8615B1B630BC422C", "Another method of applying weather within a space is the [Radial_Storm_;radialstorm] actor.\r\n\r\nA Radial Storm is a circular space, within which a single [weather_settings_preset_;weatherpreset] is applied. Radial Storms are limited to just this circular shape, unlike a [Weather_Override_Volume_;weatheroverridevolume] which can be an arbitrary shape defined by a spline.\r\n\r\nThe unique benefit of a Radial Storm is that it can render its own local effects and draw its own local cloud coverage. This means when you\'re outside of the storm, you can  see the storm in the distance, as a formation of clouds, with fog and obscured lightning underneath. Radial Storms are also built for their presence in the level to be dynamic. You can spawn one in at runtime and have it fade in and out, both in its effect on weather state and the visible effects. A Radial Storm can also move linearly across the level.\r\n\r\nNote, the effects visible from outside of a Radial Storm are limited to the [Volumetric_Clouds_;volumetricclouds] [sky_mode_;skymode] on UDS. A Radial Storm can still be used with the other sky modes, but only as a way to affect [weather_state_;weatherstate] based on the player\'s position, like the Weather Override Volumes.\r\n\r\nRadial Storms are named as such because their features are mainly intended for stormy weather. But note you can also use them to apply any weather conditions within the radial space, including calm/clear skies."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "C5BDFB41408DCFEF3B00239E7F96CF4C", "***"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "467C85014741D73515814980627A20C7", "^Radial Storm Spawning"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "0AF997E74B9C8243D2330BB535995DD4", ">On UDW, in the Radial Storm Spawning category, you\'ll find settings to enable periodic randomized spawning of Radial Storm actors during play. UDW will spawn radial storms one at a time, placing them and moving them so they will pass over the player\'s location. The weather preset the storms use can be determined by the current season, similar to Random Weather Variation."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "0A86D28D448BE83EED8C58A26D09F93A", "***"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "8CE5EA024F8AAFE3A74418829CAB26C5", "The Radial Storm actor can also be spawned in manually or placed in the level directly. You don\'t need to rely on UDW\'s spawning logic if you don\'t want to. The functions on the Radial Storm actor for controlling it at runtime include:"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "407A41FA437910C8619E8BA4840A5876", "^Fade In Storm"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "B62F567445C99891B040B1BF05E98DC1", ">Starts the storm fading, from 0 alpha up to 1, over the fade duration. You can call this after spawning a Radial Storm at runtime."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "96AF62624E0D2CEF3877248F61D80F65", "^Fade Out Storm"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "A0E4234E429D30656BBD95849E14208A", ">Similar to the Fade In function, but fades the storm out over time, and destroys the actor at the end of the fade."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "DB28526444C538F97DB1EDAF2D222C72", "^Move Storm Over Time"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "4DCDA1C94B1DDA5DA9CEF0A7CD75B824", ">Call this function to have the storm move across the level, to a target position, over a duration. Optionally, this function can also fade out and destroy the actor at the end of the movement path."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "F3DBC6E8422985CA494221B7F7CA693A", "[IMAGE]\r\nhttps://imagedelivery.net/dJ8zT5MNjUXoua7duc582w/da0fae7d-f0ba-4a09-60b3-6da31fc50800/public\r\nIn this example, a Radial Storm actor is spawned. It will then fade in for 30 seconds while moving across the level for 200 seconds. For the last 30 seconds of the movement it will fade out and destroy."))` |
| `EntryTitle_4_4B2C1546415E1329EC06F8B28CB05DF9` | `FText` | `NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "B788B9D04C1895D52206E7B472BC0369", "Radial Storms")` |
| `Keywords_8_5ACC585649ABDE1192D0EAB5258A2665` | `TArray` | `("radial storm","radial storms","storm","storms","radial","circular weather","weather area")` |

When you drag it into your scene, it will be a small straight line, but you can edit the spline to change the length and shape of the line. Move and rotate the spline points, and add more spline points by right clicking on the spline path.\r\n\r\nThe collision and appearance of the particles this actor spawns will be controlled using the settings for rain particles on UDW."))` |

### Row `RandomWeather`

| Field | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Category_12_A3CA532A4207111301CC0DB004E1A0F4` | `int32` | `1` |
| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "E8993E8E4D95BCDAA24BCD86FEA047F9", "[Random_Weather_Variation_;randomweathervariation] can change the weather state periodically, selecting a new [weather_preset_;weatherpreset] based on [season_;season] and a set of probability maps. It\'s controlled from the Random Weather Variation category on UDW.\r\n\r\nTo enable Random Weather Variation, change the Random Weather Variation setting on UDW to select a timing mode. There are three timing modes: Random Interval, Daily, and Hourly. These determine when the random weather will change.\r\n\r\nIf Random Interval is the selected timing mode, Random Weather Change Interval controls the min and max of how long the system will hold on a given weather preset before picking a new random one to transition to.\r\n\r\nIf Hourly or Daily are selected for the timing mode, the random changes will happen based on the time that passes on Ultra Dynamic Sky. Random Weather Change Hour controls what point in the day the change will happen when using Daily mode.\r\n\r\nTransition Length is the fraction of the interval between changes devoted to transitioning from the old weather to the new weather.\r\n\r\nThe maps of Weather Type Probabilities contain the weather presets and a corresponding probability value. This value is proportional to the rest of the values in the map. Meaning, if one type is set to 5 and the rest are set to 1, that type will be 5 times more likely to be picked. The map used will depend on the current season, controlled from the Season category."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "A54DCA874661E2857D9AEA9BF07A58CC", "[IMAGE]\r\nhttps://imagedelivery.net/dJ8zT5MNjUXoua7duc582w/214183fa-5f60-42d9-c44c-cddc18c25a00/public\r\nIn this example probability map, Rain would be twice as likely to be selected as Partly Cloudy, each time a new random weather is selected."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "FF2082F34D78768ED13AC9B9E150FC9B", "\"Begin Play Weather is Random\" controls how the random weather will start when you play the level. If this is true, a starting random weather will be selected. If this is false, the weather will start with the same weather shown in the level editor, and change after the first interval has passed.\r\n\r\nYou can also apply a [climate_preset_;climatepreset] from here, which will use real world climate data to create probability maps which suit that climate, and also set the temperature ranges in the Temperature category.\r\n\r\nYou can use the [Change_Weather_;changeweather] function at runtime to change from Random Weather Variation to a specific static preset. If you need to change back to the Random Weather Variation, call \"Change to Random Weather Variation\"."))` |
| `EntryTitle_4_4B2C1546415E1329EC06F8B28CB05DF9` | `FText` | `NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "980E93A0460403C73A1A14A00DFDB8F7", "Random Weather Variation")` |

| `Category_12_A3CA532A4207111301CC0DB004E1A0F4` | `int32` | `0` |
| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "012CFBD342A76B21322D2A9FBF8BA88B", "When rendering out a sequence using the movie render queue, first make sure to change [Project_Mode_;projectmode] on UDS to \"Cinematic / Offline\". This configures the sky for maximum quality at [runtime;runtime] , while also disabling many optimizations that are useful only in real-time rendering scenarios. If rendering a movie using the [path_tracer;pathtracer] , see the section in this document on using UDS with the path tracer.\r\n\r\nIf your project does need real-time performance at runtime normally , be sure to turn Project Mode back to Game / Real-time after completing your movie render, or game performance will be severely compromised.\r\n\r\nNote the Cinematic / Offline Mode category on UDS, which has additional settings to adjust how quality is affected when rendering in that mode."))` |

### Row `SampleTemp`

| Field | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Category_12_A3CA532A4207111301CC0DB004E1A0F4` | `int32` | `1` |
| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "5A3C1DE9472C62FE20FE2491347E0092", "There is a function on UDW called \"Get Current Temperature\", which you can call to sample the current temperature in Fahrenheit or Celsius. This value is generated in a simple and predictable way where temperature is a product of weather and never the other way around. The settings for this are found in the Temperature category on UDW."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "8486D68C437217CE0CE4E0889CFC1B42", "[IMAGE]\r\nhttps://imagedelivery.net/dJ8zT5MNjUXoua7duc582w/96ce7700-5e80-4b51-2b8e-33d809e23f00/public\r\nThe function to sample the temperature from UDW."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "BF6D7B6D4D21909D35A10B86F7BE256C", "^How Temperature is Calculated"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "57F8290C400FF1C7742842BECC6CA93A", ">- The system starts with a value of 0, and adds to it using all the values labeled Temperature Bias in the Temperature category. These values use factors like [Time_of_Day_;timeofday] and [weather_state_;weatherstate] to add or subtract from this starting value.\r\n\r\n- The resulting value is then mapped from a range of -1 to 1 over to the Min and Max range for the current [season;season] .\r\n\r\n- A slowly changing random value is added to the temperature value, scaled by the Randomize Temperature setting.\r\n\r\n- If an option other than Global is selected for Sample Location when calling the function, location based effects will be applied as well. Temperature Volumes in the level will be sampled (see below), and Interior Temperature will be applied based on the amount the location is occluded by surrounding collision."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "108C68094B25824415C2738173739E7E", "***"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "F0645CEB4830A41ED8C723865AF12D22", "Note, if using [Weather_Override_Volumes;weatheroverridevolume] , these will apply their own temperature ranges while the player is inside them. You can adjust the temperature ranges it applies from the WOV\'s settings, or disable this behavior there."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "5A40F8184ABB2EF0ADF1CDB2E2959846", "***"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "A1CFF42B463D5AB48B5424B37064E343", "^Temperature Volumes"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "7BE4E589468A6B83C7319EB9F3F8AA89", "> The actor class Temperature Volume, found in the Blueprints/Weather_Effects folder, can be placed in the level to have custom local effects on temperature. For example, you could place a Temperature Volume actor around a fire, with a positive Temperature Offset setting, and temperature sampled within the volume would be higher."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "AE8FA98D4029CC11D2C6539AC1EDEE99", "***"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "3C594EA54DBD98DAC00470994A700032", "^Show Temperature Onscreen"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "B93122444CEC8F50415F74B60CC40ED3", ">There is a widget included which can sample and display the current temperature from UDW on screen. The widget is \"UDW Thermometer\" and can be found in the widget designer in the Ultra Dynamic Sky Widgets category."))` |
| `EntryTitle_4_4B2C1546415E1329EC06F8B28CB05DF9` | `FText` | `NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "19EF28874E712272C12A539F19D76EB6", "Sampling Temperature")` |

| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "653CF3BF4504DBC63C8A788D5545419B", "Here are some tips for animating the sky using sequencer."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "C74EC6F14D335F8FE9980AB1228E8400", "^Keyframing Time of Day"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "422C097645AAE77402D97CAE129E224D", "> To animate [Time_of_Day_;timeofday] directly, you should disable the Animate Time of Day setting on UDS, and keyframe the Time of Day variable. When animating with the Time of Day variable, it\'s okay to go past 2400. The system will understand this and proceed forward in time with a new day."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "3BE603644E3EE27A7D686BAB28FCDFDA", "^Keyframing Cloud Coverage or Fog"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "8D4444004F9899D5DE090D9754269202", "> To animate the cloudiness or fogginess, you can keyframe the [Cloud_Coverage_;udscloudcoverage] or [Fog_;udsfog] variables on UDS, but only if you don\'t have an Ultra Dynamic Weather actor in your scene. If you do, you should keyframe the Cloud Coverage and Fog variables on UDW instead, using its manual weather state. (See the sequencer section in Weather for more info about animating weather state on UDW)"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "430BD0E94CD1D221A49728B85291A850", "^Keyframing Cloud Movement"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "A741E3EE4DB6F31D406F599D76CFD409", "> To directly animate cloud movement, first set Cloud Speed to 0. Disable \"Randomize Cloud Formation on Run\" and \"Clouds Move with Time of Day\" as well. Then in sequencer, animate using the Cloud Phase variable. This will allow you to directly control cloud movement in a way that will play back the same way every time."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "4C303ACD415BB00F1C64629542B460E3", "^Keyframing Other Variables"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "90B4D66942383686A58311A35B7BC31E", ">Not every variable on UDS is reapplied dynamically at [runtime;runtime] , in the way that would be needed to animate the value in a cinematic. Many are though, and all of the UDS variables that will work without additional steps are exposed to be keyframed.\r\n\r\nIf you want to try keyframing additional variables that are not exposed by default, you\'ll need to mark them as exposed. Open UDS in the blueprint editor, find the variable in the My Blueprint panel, and check Expose to Cinematics on its variable details.\r\n\r\nAny variables you expose manually like that will probably not update with the keyframe at runtime, but you could try calling the relevant Static Properties function every frame of the animation, and that should work to force values to update."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "8A82240448F0F0D275B5B3BB1112B7F3", "For tips about animating weather, see the section about sequencer in the Weather section of the readme."))` |

### Row `SequenceWeather`

| Field | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Category_12_A3CA532A4207111301CC0DB004E1A0F4` | `int32` | `1` |
| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "87C4C64C42A99F6DADEFBA9F6B1785F2", "Here are some tips for how the weather system can be animated using sequencer."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "237784AB4CE65B7D6C6737BB1E630992", "^Keyframing the Weather State"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "795831C84FEF51B95051849072481C3A", ">To animate the current [weather_state_;weatherstate] manually using sequencer, you\'ll want to use the Manual Weather State, keyframing the variables in that category. See the entry on the Manual Weather State for more info on using that."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "78F178BE46EDC70D9D52E4927A8F3399", "^Keyframing the Material Effects"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "AFFFEA0342120FADA50F72B0D391E483", ">If you\'re keyframing the Material Wetness, Material Snow Coverage, or Material Dust Coverage directly, you\'ll need to make one change to have those keyframes work the same at runtime as they do in your sequence. In the Material Effects category, disable \"Simulate Changing Material State Over Time\". This will make it so at [runtime_;runtime] the material effects show exactly as they\'re keyframed at each frame, instead of changing gradually with weather state."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "06457B2745340AF8BAC445ABF981DE24", "^Keyframing Cloud Movement"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "ECD3A9CF461D0A0C8116E6B6623BBF4F", ">To animate cloud movement in a way that will play back the same every time: First, set Cloud Speed to 0 on UDS. Then, turn off Randomize Cloud Formation On Run, in Cloud Movement on UDS. Then in Sequencer, keyframe the Cloud Phase variable on UDS. This will allow directly controlling cloud movement with keyframes."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "0D1F28E2421E01A31C37F184F47D711C", "^Keyframing a Lightning Flash"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "2D7A96DD41FCB09C13342DB602FFE5A4", ">To spawn a lightning flash from a sequence, add UDW to the sequence and create an Event>Trigger track on UDW. Add a keyframe to the track, and right click it to see its properties. For its Endpoint, search for Flash Lightning under Quick Bind. With that function bound, you can configure the inputs for the lightning flash (it\'s custom location, seed, etc) from the keyframe\'s properties. Make sure to also check Call in Editor in the properties if you want the lightning flash to be previewed in the sequence editor."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "421E1C9B47E5028BF66438A9C40370C3", "^Rendering a Movie"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "7B1FFE0946AC9F18C81CD089BAF652C6", ">Take note of the Project Mode setting on UDS, if you need to render a movie for offline playback. Change that setting on UDS to \"Cinematic / Offline\", to force max quality for the sky rendering and force both blueprints to update completely every frame at runtime. See the rendering entry in the sky section for more info.\r\n\r\nAlso, if you are rendering your movie with the path tracer, make sure to read the documentation entry on UDS\' path tracer support and how to configure for it."))` |
| `EntryTitle_4_4B2C1546415E1329EC06F8B28CB05DF9` | `FText` | `NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "03A65D96404F2BAEFFF3BD84B22CD374", "Using Weather with Sequencer")` |

| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "393927FB42E66D13E390388D0B2CCBFF", "Change the [Time_of_Day_;timeofday] property in Basic Controls to adjust the time of day the system will start with. You can also enable an option to start with a random time, from the Animate Time of Day category.\r\n\r\nFor directly controlling Time of Day at [runtime;runtime] , there are several ways you can do that:"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "9C8677B14BFD102DC50FE8A78AD258E8", ">- Simply setting Time of Day on UDS at runtime will instantly change the time directly.\r\n\r\n- You can call the functions called \"Set Time with Time Code\" or \"Set Date and Time\" to use common time/date structures to set the time with hours/minutes values.\r\n\r\n- You can call the function \"Transition Time of Day\", to start the time animating to a target value over a specified duration. This is useful if you want to have time pass quickly to a particular point."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "F3B8193A4830B82321DF618E5FF27E86", "[IMAGE]\r\nhttps://imagedelivery.net/dJ8zT5MNjUXoua7duc582w/517cfb19-7c49-4dbc-f515-97960bbe7700/public\r\nFour functions you can call from your classes to set the time on Ultra Dynamic Sky."))` |

### Row `SettingUpSky`

| Field | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Category_12_A3CA532A4207111301CC0DB004E1A0F4` | `int32` | `0` |
| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "FDEC16734E420B04EBE4A585E6338C4B", "First, make sure you\'ve removed any existing sky and cleared the following out of your level:"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "4805EC6E40C209C4B8170B8AEF2E1A16", ">- [Directional_Lights;directionallight] \r\n- [Sky_Light;skylight] \r\n- [Exponential_Height_Fog;heightfog] \r\n- [Sky_Atmosphere;skyatmosphere] \r\n- [Volumetric_Cloud;volumetricclouds] "),INVTEXT("With all of these removed, if there is still some ambient light present, that probably means there\'s still [static_light_;staticlight] left over in the level\'s lightmaps, so run a lighting build (from the Build dropdown on the main toolbar) to clear that out.\r\n\r\nDrag the Ultra Dynamic Sky actor into your scene from the Blueprints folder. You should see the sky with its default configuration of daytime lighting with volumetric clouds.\r\n\r\nTypically you should place UDS at ground level. If you want to change the height of the clouds, use Bottom Altitude in the Volumetric Clouds category instead of moving the actor.\r\n\r\nNote, depending on the context, the editor may need to compile shaders for UDS before all of its features become visible. The editor should indicate this is happening, and it can potentially take a while depending on your system specs."))` |
| `EntryTitle_4_4B2C1546415E1329EC06F8B28CB05DF9` | `FText` | `NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "F7B8866D40E43576B98E3085C1805D98", "Adding Ultra Dynamic Sky to Your Level")` |

| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "2637B7724C947888BB56069377133C44", "If [Color_Mode_;colormode] is set to [Simplified_Color;simplifiedcolor] , then the main controls of sky color will be found in the Simplified Color category. Here are some of they key settings:"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "6134584B4DA91CBF03EB739894C04AB9", ">- The color variables in Simplified Color control the base sky color, as well as the light and dark color of the 2D Dynamic Clouds and Static Clouds. (For control of volumetric cloud color, see the Volumetric Cloud category.)\r\n\r\n- The Directional Intensity float curve controls how much the intensity of the [directional_light_;directionallight] is dimmed down as it nears the horizon.\r\n\r\n- The Directional Light Scattering color curve controls how the directional light color is filtered as it nears the horizon.\r\n\r\n- The Sun and Moon atmosphere LUT textures are used by the sky material to derive atmospheric colors from camera vector and the orientation of the sun/moon light. They are volume textures authored in a pretty involved process to closely match sky atmosphere colors by default. If you want to modify them at all, I would recommend just doing color transforms to the included textures."))` |
| `EntryTitle_4_4B2C1546415E1329EC06F8B28CB05DF9` | `FText` | `NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "294B44704488D19CF78631BB96694FD3", "Simplified Color")` |

### Row `Simulation`

| Field | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Category_12_A3CA532A4207111301CC0DB004E1A0F4` | `int32` | `0` |
| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "CA93A73C46BD92D6C6048B83137EED99", "UDS has features to position the sun, moon and stars using real world coordinates and date. These options are found in the Simulation category.\r\n\r\nTo enable them, just check Simulate Real Sun, Simulate Real Moon, and Simulate Real Stars. Each of these can also be enabled individually as needed."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "A0C6BBF540F6FE39A42A319BD62C7111", ">- Simulate Real Sun and Simulate Real Moon simply override the default logic for the positioning of the sun and moon. All of the settings for positioning/path in the Sun and Moon categories will be overridden (except for Manually Position, which takes priority over the Simulation). Simulate Real Moon also controls Moon Phase.\r\n\r\n- Simulate Real Stars will change what texture is used for the stars. By default a simple tiling stars texture is used. With Simulate Real Stars enabled, a 360 degree star map will be used instead. Both of these texture settings are exposed to be changed out in the Stars category."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "432C2BDC47EA82CD6F549AB289FA1B9E", "The simulated location is determined using the Latitude and Longitude values. Also make sure to set the Time Zone to the correct UTC offset for the location, so that [Time_of_Day_;timeofday] will be interpreted correctly as local to this location. You can also select a city preset, which will apply latitude, longitude, time zone, and daylight savings settings in one step.\r\n\r\nThe year, month and day control the date of the simulation. At [runtime;runtime] , the date will increment forward every night at midnight, like you would expect.\r\n\r\nNorth Yaw can be adjusted to change what world space direction corresponds to north in the simulation. It\'s a value in degrees, rotating the simulation clockwise. By default, north is toward positive X."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "F7227152497F73233701BCA5C83E0954", "***"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "6EC3F36B4D2C12AFC8664987A7FA8775", "^Notes on the Simulation Accuracy"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "32A177ED4C77605D5C09BC94A1781B6C", ">Because the complete versions of the appropriate astronomical algorithms would be very expensive to calculate with blueprint math, what I\'ve created here is my own approximation. It leaves out complicating nuances such as the eccentricity of the earth\'s orbit, or the irregularity of the earth\'s shape. That said, I\'ve done a lot of back and forth testing, and my approximations of the sun\'s position were never more than a little over a degree off from the results given by the complete algorithm, and that deviation is a worst case scenario. Typically the deviation was only in fractions of a degree. Again, based on my own tests. You may find edge cases where the deviation is worse. Still, I think the accuracy of the sun is sufficient for almost all practical applications.\r\n\r\nThe accuracy of the Moon\'s position is more variable than the sun\'s. The Moon\'s orbit is calibrated using it\'s position in 2017. So, any date within several decades of that should be generally accurate. At the very least, the moon should generally appear in the correct constellation and have the right phase."))` |
| `EntryTitle_4_4B2C1546415E1329EC06F8B28CB05DF9` | `FText` | `NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "9E7AD08044FB656CF577F99FBDB6DC26", "Simulation of Real World Sun, Moon and Stars")` |
| `Keywords_8_5ACC585649ABDE1192D0EAB5258A2665` | `TArray` | `("simulation","simulate","date","time","sun","moon","realistic","coordinates","latitude","longitude","real","astronomical","stars","constellations","world","earth","sim")` |
| `SubCategoryHeading_15_F6EBA06941D30788CC14989999E6C63B` | `bool` | `False` |

### Row `SimulationTime`

| Field | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Category_12_A3CA532A4207111301CC0DB004E1A0F4` | `int32` | `0` |
| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "97C1E2584051999D5DFABE9E27E651AF", "If Simulate Real Sun is enabled, [Time_of_Day_;timeofday] will behave differently in some ways to suit the needs of the [simulation;simulation] . Also the simulation has some specific features which interpret or change how time is handled."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "456AC67D4B824BF868D5708FE9105A81", ">- If Animate Time of Day is enabled, the speed of time will not be determined by Day Length and Night Length. Instead, it will be determined by Simulation Speed, in the Simulation category. This value scales the speed of time, with 1 being roughly realistic speed.\r\n\r\n- Options for daylight savings time can be found in the Simulation category. If enabled, Time of Day will be interpreted with DST within the range of the year set by the DST start and end times in the advanced dropdown of the Simulation category.\r\n\r\n- Use System Time, in the Simulation category, will set the Time of Day and date values using the UTC time from the system clock, offset by the selected Time Zone. This feature can also be used without making use of any of the Simulation features."))` |

Here are some of the key settings:"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "AA9DD3A542B53BB3B31D74969B4B8535", ">- The Rayleigh Scattering settings are what chiefly determine the main color of the sky. It can be adjusted for day, night, and dawn/dusk individually.\r\n\r\n- The Sunset/Sunrise and Twilight values control the Absorption setting on the sky atmosphere component. | Field | Type | Value |

| `Category_12_A3CA532A4207111301CC0DB004E1A0F4` | `int32` | `0` |
| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "0663D4A641DD13FFC1D360A6AAE9F02A", "Ultra Dynamic Sky has a Dust category, which can be used to imitate the air being full of dust/smoke/other particulates.\r\n\r\nDust Amount is used to affect the fog density, height falloff, and fog color. ### Row `SkyGlow`

| Field | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Category_12_A3CA532A4207111301CC0DB004E1A0F4` | `int32` | `0` |
| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "AB28C92143A612D633CEA195A8547D61", "The Sky Glow category has options which add additional light to the night sky independent of the moon/sun.\r\n\r\nNight Sky Glow adds uniform light to the sky material and subtly lights the volumetric clouds from above. The idea is to imitate the effect of ambient star light and general atmosphere glow, but it can be increased as needed to add additional minimum illumination to the night sky, to keep things from getting too dark without moonlight.\r\n\r\nLight Pollution adds light to the sky material and softly illuminates volumetric clouds from below. This is to imitate the effect of city lighting on the atmosphere."))` |

### Row `SkyLight`

| Field | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Category_12_A3CA532A4207111301CC0DB004E1A0F4` | `int32` | `0` |
| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "5DA0F2E94D9C4BECEACBD1AA1EFA69BF", "In the Sky Light category, [Sky_Light_Mode_;skylightmode] determines the source of the [sky_light_;skylight] cubemap and how its intensity and color will be controlled by UDS.\r\nThese are the Sky Light Modes and how they work:"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "DE95A7FA4895F7EECA8DE8BDFA766704", ">1. Capture Based - The sky light will generate a cubemap by capturing the sky. By default, this method uses the real time capture option, which UDS exposes to a setting in the Sky Light category.\r\n\r\n2. Custom Cubemap - A simple static cubemap texture, set using the Sky Light Cubemap option below.\r\n\r\n3. Cubemap with Dynamic Color Tinting - This method uses a flat gray cubemap and tints it dynamically with the fog color to align well with the time of day. This option is good for performance in projects with dynamic time of day, as the ambient light is dynamic without requiring recapturing, and supports all platforms."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "3CE3023546C36DD84070718D4B37D36B", "You can also use the Sky Light Color Multiplier settings to tint the color differently based on [Time_of_Day;timeofday] . Note that these color multipliers can also be set to values higher than 1 and this will scale the light intensity proportionally at that time."))` |
| `EntryTitle_4_4B2C1546415E1329EC06F8B28CB05DF9` | `FText` | `NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "CF090B694DE63B0E5B133BBFFCF0B86C", "Sky Light")` |
| `Keywords_8_5ACC585649ABDE1192D0EAB5258A2665` | `TArray` | `("sky light","skylight","capture","cubemap","hdri","light","ambient")` |

### Row `SkyMode`

| Field | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Category_12_A3CA532A4207111301CC0DB004E1A0F4` | `int32` | `0` |
| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "BC499EA74B349C5E67077F818DFEB1FF", "In Basic Controls on UDS, there is a setting called [Sky_Mode;skymode] . This mainly controls the type of clouds (or volumetric aurora) in use. Here is a quick explanation of each option:"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "6F6AAC6348ABE2C56D3300A90109116E", ">1. [Volumetric_Clouds_;volumetricclouds] - Enabled by default, this sky mode uses a field of full 3D clouds. This can offer the most realistic visuals, but at a performance cost that may be too much for some projects/platforms.\r\n\r\n2. [Static_Clouds_;staticclouds] - Designed to mimic the look of the volumetric clouds but as a static cloud texture. Much lower performance cost than volumetric clouds.\r\n\r\n3. [2D_Dynamic_Clouds_;2ddynamicclouds] - Dynamic clouds drawn using panning 2D textures.\r\n\r\n4. No Clouds - This mode uses no dynamic clouds at all.\r\n\r\n5. [Volumetric_Aurora_;volumetricaurora] - Sacrifices clouds to render full 3D aurora effects. Adjustable using the settings in the Aurora category.\r\n\r\n6. [Space_;spacemode] - For scenes set in outer space, with no planet/ground beneath the viewer. Disables all clouds, atmosphere, sky coloring, leaving only sun, moon and stars.\r\n"))` |
| `EntryTitle_4_4B2C1546415E1329EC06F8B28CB05DF9` | `FText` | `NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "FF41AD564F1CBCE8F7C7488FA7B0979D", "Sky Mode")` |

### Row `SkyUtilityMatFunctions`

| Field | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Category_12_A3CA532A4207111301CC0DB004E1A0F4` | `int32` | `0` |
| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "50AA23FE456457A5B303649846694E96", "UDS includes a few material functions to serve some basic utilities in materials, controlled by the state of the UDS blueprint automatically. These can be found by searching for them in the material palette, in any material."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "E7C045D6404FABB9004E10BA59B7A647", "^Day to Night Float/Color"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "98726BD24F13B7BC935BCDBDC835E251", "> There are two functions, \"Day to Night Float\" and \"Day to Night Color\". These take in two values, and interpolate from one to the other based on if the sun is up or down. There are inputs to offset the threshold above or below the horizon, and widen or sharpen the range used for the transition."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "16E3D6914C509E4F839B2D89E1FDF6C3", "^Active Sun or Moon Vector"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "EC7F8F224A1C305F3F4812B526A00C4F", "> The function \"Active Sun or Moon Vector\" outputs a unit vector pointing in the direction of the sun light, when the sun is up, and in the direction of the moon light, when only the moon is up. A second 0-1 value is output which goes down to 0 at the moment the vector changes from one to the other, to help mask any effect which uses the vector."))` |

### Row `SoundOcclusion`

| Field | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Category_12_A3CA532A4207111301CC0DB004E1A0F4` | `int32` | `1` |
| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "BF5949AE4D877FDB579943999373A467", "The sound effects on UDW are affected by a simple system of sound occlusion by default, which periodically sends out traces from the camera location and adjusts sound volume and low pass filter frequency (how muffled the sound is) if the player is in an enclosed space. This behavior can be disabled or adjusted from the Sound Occlusion category.\r\n\r\nThe Player Occlusion system on UDS is what handles querying the scene collision to calculate how occluded the sound should be. You can find the settings for how it calculates occlusion in the Player Occlusion category on UDS.\r\n\r\nYou can also place the [UDS_Occlusion_Volume_;udsocclusionvolume] actor, found in Blueprints/Occlusion, to force specific spaces to be fully occluded and always attenuate weather sounds. Note the option in Player Occlusion for \"Occlusion Sampling Mode\" which affects if these volumes will be sampled.\r\n\r\nAlso note the component class called UDS Occlusion Portal. If any of these exist in the area around the occlusion sampling location, they will be traced against, and can negate occlusion if the trace is unobstructed. For example, you could have an occlusion portal component placed for an open door or window, allowing outside weather sound effects to enter the space in a more natural way.\r\n\r\nIf you want your own sound sources in the level to be affected by the volume attenuation of the sound occlusion, you can set them to use the sound class \"UDS Outdoor Sound\"."))` |
| `EntryTitle_4_4B2C1546415E1329EC06F8B28CB05DF9` | `FText` | `NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "737F1EA644CF98E6E73CABADA9DE1B22", "Sound Occlusion")` |
| `Keywords_8_5ACC585649ABDE1192D0EAB5258A2665` | `TArray` | `("sound occlusion","sound effects","weather sounds","interior","occlusion","muffle","quiet","wind sound","audio")` |
| `SubCategoryHeading_15_F6EBA06941D30788CC14989999E6C63B` | `bool` | `False` |
| `SuggestedEntries_19_9776F58E45A513F145D90BBE28516AA1` | `TArray` | `("WeatherSounds","PlayerOcclusion")` |

### Row `SpaceLayer`

| Field | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Category_12_A3CA532A4207111301CC0DB004E1A0F4` | `int32` | `0` |
| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "F01CDD6B4FD1C1073DFCEF885B38B3CC", "UDS can render additional planets and moons, to the sky layer, correctly composited so they block stars, but are obscured behind clouds and aurora.\r\n\r\nThe place to do this is the Space Layer category on UDS. You can either manually add planets to the Planets / Moons array in that category, or you can start with one of the presets by selecting something for \"Add Planet / Moon Preset\".\r\n\r\nWithin the Planets / Moons array, you can customize the look and behavior of each planet.\r\n\r\nAll of the settings have tooltips, but here are a few key ones to note:"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "56626AEC4AA9E61CA44AD4BFC531730E", ">- Parent controls what the planet will move with. It can be parented to the sun, the moon, or it can be left unparented so it doesn\'t move, or could potentially be moved manually at runtime by manipulating the transform of the components in the Space Roots array on UDS.\r\n\r\n- Relative Rotation rotates the orientation of the planet, relative to what it\'s been parented to.\r\n\r\n- Scale sets the visual scale of the planet.\r\n\r\n- The Terminator settings refer to the solar terminator, the line between the light and dark sides of the planet.\r\n\r\n- The Light Vector controls where the light source determining the light/dark side of the planet will come from. The sun, the moon, or the custom vector.\r\n\r\n- The Glow settings control an additional element, which renders a diffuse atmospheric glow around the planet. The brightness depends on how much of the lit side is facing the camera, and is scaled with the setting Space Glow Brightness in the Space Layer category."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "8F9388404F4CBA15DFE5CA9840113CC1", "The space layer draws these additional planets into the sky material using the dbuffer. So Dbuffer Decals should be enabled in your project (or Mobile DBuffer Decals for the mobile renderer), and need to be supported by the platform, for these planets/moons to be rendered."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "4A07CB224B06D1845E9E59AA5EE31DCC", "Also in the Space Layer category, you\'ll find an option to enable a layer of Nebula, rendered into the sky material the same way as the planets/moons. This nebula effect is noise based, and has parameters exposed to adjust its noise settings, colors, and intensity."))` |
| `EntryTitle_4_4B2C1546415E1329EC06F8B28CB05DF9` | `FText` | `NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "9E67C59147CD703A1D0336AC96BD6A3D", "Adding Planets / Moons / Nebula Using the Space Layer")` |
| `Keywords_8_5ACC585649ABDE1192D0EAB5258A2665` | `TArray` | `("space","planet","moon","moons","planets","space layer")` |
| `SubCategoryHeading_15_F6EBA06941D30788CC14989999E6C63B` | `bool` | `False` |
| `SuggestedEntries_19_9776F58E45A513F145D90BBE28516AA1` | `TArray` | `("SkyMode","SunandMoonPath")` |

### Row `Stars`

This can be replaced with the Tiling Stars texture variable.\r\n\r\nIf Simulate Real Stars is enabled in the [Simulation_;simulation] category, a much higher res 360 degree star map will be used. This can be replaced with the Real Stars texture variable.\r\n\r\nIn the Stars category, you can also find settings for the stars color, intensity, and how much they imitate an atmospheric twinkling effect."))` |

This texture has different lighting angles packed into it to allow the clouds to approximate a simple lighting effect as the sun and moon change orientation.\r\n\r\nThe Static Clouds category has a few settings for changing out the texture used by the static clouds, and controlling its rotation.\r\n\r\nThere are three static clouds textures included, but you can also create your own custom ones using a special editor utility. The Static Clouds Authoring Tool can render the volumetric clouds on UDS to create a new static clouds texture. Run this tool from the Ultra Dynamic Sky dropdown on the level editor toolbar, or by running the editor utility found in Blueprints/Tools."))` |

### Row `StaticStationary`

| Field | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Category_12_A3CA532A4207111301CC0DB004E1A0F4` | `int32` | `0` |
| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "82F36F5842293712911B038CFE17F1EB", "UDS\' default configuration uses all movable lights, but it supports [static_lighting_;staticlight] as well.\r\n\r\nTo make any of UDS\' lights static or stationary, find its mobility setting, in the UDS details. These are found in the lights\' respective categories, so Sun, Moon, and Sky Light. Make sure you set the mobility from the exposed setting, and not on the light component itself.\r\n\r\nOnce you\'ve built the level\'s lighting, you will still be able to make some changes to the sky settings, but note that any settings which alter the lights or move them around will break the lighting build and you\'ll have to build again. Also note that if your sun light is set to be static/stationary, [Time_of_Day_;timeofday] will not be able to change at runtime."))` |
| `EntryTitle_4_4B2C1546415E1329EC06F8B28CB05DF9` | `FText` | `NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "B61AF1B8473FB8CC6E8C28B0202A8294", "Using Static/Stationary Lighting")` |

### Row `SunandMoonPath`

| Field | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Category_12_A3CA532A4207111301CC0DB004E1A0F4` | `int32` | `0` |
| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "92EAA4BC4D02524CC36F87B582B84205", "By default (without using the [Simulation_;simulation] settings covered elsewhere in this document) the Sun and Moon\'s position in the sky with time will be derived using the following settings found in both the Sun and Moon categories:"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "3288467142FEA63864F07DBE0CDD06E2", ">- Yaw (Sun Yaw and Moon Yaw) - This controls the yaw of the sun or moon\'s circular path. In other words, the direction that it will set/rise. It\'s a value in degrees, rotating the path clockwise.\r\n\r\n- Pitch (Sun Pitch and Moon Pitch) - This pitches the path, so that the sun or moon\'s highest position in the sky will be lower, angled away from the zenith. It\'s also a value in degrees, with 0 meaning the sun/moon would go all the way to the top of the sky at its peak.\r\n\r\n- Vertical Offset (Sun Vertical Offset and Moon Vertical Offset) - This value can be positive or negative, to push the position of the sun or moon higher or lower, irrespective of the time.\r\n\r\n- The moon specifically also has a setting for Moon Orbit Offset which controls how the moon is offset from the sun in time. A value of 0 will have the moon\'s path be the opposite of the sun\'s, rising at night and going down during the day."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "5BAC081148EE1D0CC68BA18ED6C79643", "Again, it\'s important to note all of these values will be ignored if you\'re using the Simulation instead. See the section in these docs on the Simulation features for more information on how to control that."))` |
| `EntryTitle_4_4B2C1546415E1329EC06F8B28CB05DF9` | `FText` | `NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "0535B2A245061457205F07ACE549F160", "Adjusting Sun and Moon Movement")` |
| `Keywords_8_5ACC585649ABDE1192D0EAB5258A2665` | `TArray` | `("sun","moon","path","orbit","angle","time","yaw","pitch")` |
| `SubCategoryHeading_15_F6EBA06941D30788CC14989999E6C63B` | `bool` | `False` |

### Row `SunAppearance`

| `Category_12_A3CA532A4207111301CC0DB004E1A0F4` | `int32` | `0` |
| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "DC8F936D42B7BE33817133BE125DB3FB", "The Sun category is where you\'ll find all the settings specifically for adjusting the appearance of the sun in the sky.\r\n\r\nThe sun is rendered as a simple radial gradient, so it has settings for scale, softness, color, and intensity.\r\n\r\nSun Scale will also be used to derive the correct light source angle of the sun [directional_light;directionallight] , so the softness of the shadows and size of specular highlights will be correct for the sun\'s size in the sky. You can scale it relative to that calculated value with Sun Source Angle Scale.\r\n\r\nThe sun also has Solar Eclipse settings, to adjust what happens when the moon, or an object in the Space Layer, goes in front of the sun."))` |

### Row `SunLensFlare`

| Field | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `Category_12_A3CA532A4207111301CC0DB004E1A0F4` | `int32` | `0` |
| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "31673B5D4E12FE4CF15FD9BC6E27B82D", "UDS has its own feature to apply a filmic lens flare to the sun specifically. Note that this is a completely separate effect from the image based lens flares built into the engine as a stock post processing effect.\r\n\r\nTo enable this lens flare, just check \"Enable Sun Lens Flare\" in the Lens Flare category, and select the Lens Flare Type you want.\r\n\r\nIt is possible to build your own custom lens flare type using this same setup. In the advanced dropdown of the Lens Flare category, see the option \"Custom Lens Flare Parent Instance\". To use this, create an instance of one of the existing lens flare material instances in Materials/Material_Instances/Lens_Flares. You can adjust the textures, colors, and mapping parameters of all the lens flare elements in your custom instance and use it with that exposed Custom parent instance setting."))` |

|---|---|---|
| `Category_12_A3CA532A4207111301CC0DB004E1A0F4` | `int32` | `0` |
| `EntryText_13_1F188F814F7F03D55DA1ED8DF4CC1347` | `TArray` | `(NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "2930763945E152398B7BEB9D1E2A3B04", "UDS has [event_dispatchers_;eventdispatcher] which are called at particular times, which your actors can use to perform actions at Sunset, Sunrise, Midnight, Hourly, Every Minute, or a Custom Time.\r\n\r\nTo use them, you\'ll first need to get a reference to the UDS actor in your blueprints. A simple way to do that is to use the shared function \"Get Ultra Dynamic Sky\". Then using that reference, you can bind events in your blueprint to the dispatchers. For example \"Bind to Sunrise\" or \"Bind to Sunset\". Once they\'re bound, these events will be called by UDS at the appropriate time.\r\n\r\nNote the setting \"Time Event Dispatcher Check Period\" in the Animate Time of Day category. This sets how often these time events can potentially be called. By default events are checked for every second whenever Time of Day is actively changing."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "DD0CE9194C389A134383FFAD3A4F0A0E", "[IMAGE]\r\nhttps://imagedelivery.net/dJ8zT5MNjUXoua7duc582w/91f57434-abf0-4125-cc45-8154a6e7d300/public\r\nAn example of a basic binding. After the binding is made to a valid UDS reference, the custom event will run when the sun rises."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "32AB4C4C406EBCA416224582F87F213F", "^Sunset and Sunrise"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "4763897E44E214EE34348A91B2538361", ">By default, the Sunset and Sunrise events will fire at the minute the sun crosses the horizon. But you can offset that time to suit your needs using the \"Sunrise Event Offset\" and \"Sunset Event Offset\" settings in the Animate Time of Day category."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "1CAAFD3044AB3C4C6173B3AF9A5FBD06", "^Hourly"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "560E0073467BF8B6F545CBB15F5914A9", ">There are two hourly event dispatchers, both of which output the current hour as an integer when called. The difference is how they handle time of day being changed instantly. The \"Hourly\" event dispatcher will be called for every hour which is skipped over by an instant time change. The \"Current Hour Changed\" event dispatcher will only be called once, for the new current hour."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "86B2B6994F3B1AE4C0FCAE81C92B8B8E", "^Every Minute"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "9F8C7A1245502058A85025BE7B655836", ">The Every Minute event works similarly to Current Hour Changed, outputting the current minute as an integer, from 0-59."),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "A388436B4636F52ECF2C329B0B5522AC", "^Custom Time"),NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "3562BC924C40D815A999FBAA216BDA51", ">The Custom Time dispatcher won\'t be called at all by default. In the Animate Time of Day category, there is an empty float array called Custom Time Dispatchers. The dispatcher will be called for each value you add to this array, when Time of Day crosses that point at runtime.\r\n\r\nWhen called, the dispatcher outputs the Array Index which caused the call. This way the logic you bind to the dispatcher can tell which of the Time of Day values in the array was just passed."))` |
| `EntryTitle_4_4B2C1546415E1329EC06F8B28CB05DF9` | `FText` | `NSLOCTEXT("[62584B454EB15A1F28B05A88048C49F4]", "A41DB4A44F98C25FA4CB0EAF7FFA80B0", "Triggering Events at Specific Times")` |
| `Keywords_8_5ACC585649ABDE1192D0EAB5258A2665` | `TArray` | `("event dispatcher","sunset","sunrise","dawn","dusk","event","control","midnight","hourly")` |
